title: Normal rings descend along faithfully flat ring maps
statement: Let $R\to S$ be a faithfully flat homomorphism of commutative rings [def-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-ring-map]. If $S$ is a normal ring [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring], then $R$ is a normal ring: if every prime localization $S_{\mathfrak q}$ is a domain integrally closed in its fraction field, then so is every prime localization $R_{\mathfrak p}$. No Noetherian, domain, finite-type or locality hypothesis is imposed; the zero ring is not faithfully flat over a nonzero ring, and $R=S=0$ is permitted (no primes).
